Eight baskets with exactly three apples hold eight times three, twenty-four apples. Eighty minus twenty-four leaves fifty-six apples. Twenty-two minus eight leaves fourteen baskets.
Those fourteen baskets must not hold exactly three, so each needs at least four. Fifty-six divided by fourteen is four, exactly four each. It works, so choice number one is out.
